newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran tells Kuwait it opposes U.S. forces in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Iran tells Kuwait it opposes U.S. forces in Gulf.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Tuesday blasted a U.S. military deployment in the Gulf, telling a Kuwaiti minister that regional states should provide for their own security.

"Conditions in neighbouring states in the Persian Gulf require that security be insured by regional states," Tehran radio quoted Rafsanjani as telling visiting Kuwaiti Communications, Electricity and Water Minister Jassem al-Oun.

He was apparently referring to Kuwait which has invited 3,000 U.S. ground troops to boost its defences and allowed U.S. Stealth bombers to operate from its territory in the latest confrontation between Washington and Baghdad.
"Neighbouring states should not provide an excuse for the presence of foreigners who only seek their illegitimate interests," Rafsanjani added.
Iran, the Gulf's dominant non-Arab power, has condemned U.S. missile strikes on Iraq and the American military buildup.
Tehran has also blasted Baghdad, saying it provided Washington with an excuse when it launched an incursion in Kurdish northern Iraq last month.

Oun flew to Iran on Monday at the start of a four-nation tour to rally support for Kuwait's policy of cooperation with the United States against Iraq. He will also visit Lebanon, Libya and non-Arab Turkey.
Other senior Kuwaiti officials have already visited several 1991 Gulf War Arab allies and Russia to explain Kuwait's stand and the need for the U.S. military buildup in the Gulf.
